title: The Trinity (canonical, T-02)
summary: This work presents the Trinity as the root axiom and derives the four debts (existence, distinction, relation, orientation) as absolved in God. It includes formal claims about a Lean-verified quaternion EM/Trinity isomorphism and a proposed truth operator. The document is largely theological and philosophical, with some physics bridges that are marked as open or analogical. The main risks are overclaiming the physics connections and treating theological assertions as formal derivations.

claims.claim_text: Before anything is assumed, Someone is: the Trinity is the self-sufficient ground of all reality.
claims.support: Before there was time... there was love. A Father, a Son, and the Spirit between them—one being, three persons.
claims.required_concession: This is a declared starting premise, not a conclusion.

claims.claim_text: The Trinity is one being, three persons, with real distinction and mutual indwelling.
claims.support: One being, three distinct centers of consciousness, love, and will.
claims.required_concession: This is an assumed theological axiom.

claims.claim_text: The four debts (existence, distinction, relation, orientation) are assumed by every worldview and cannot be derived by any system.
claims.support: Strip any system down to its floor, and four assumptions are sitting there, used by everyone, derived by no one.
claims.required_concession: This is a philosophical argument, not a formal proof.

claims.claim_text: The four debts are absolved in the Trinity: existence as aseity, distinction as persons, relation as perichoresis, orientation as love.
claims.support: We hold one axiom—God—and the four dissolve into Him.
claims.required_concession: This is a theological interpretation, not a formal derivation.

claims.claim_text: The Trinity is the structural minimum for truth to be fully real, requiring being, expression, and witness.
claims.support: A solitary god could not be truth in the full sense—because truth requires expression and witness.
claims.required_concession: This is a theological argument, not a formal proof.

claims.claim_text: Truth is a three-mode operator: Truth = (Being) × (Expression) × (Witness).
claims.support: Truth is a three-mode operator that acts on the space of possibilities.
claims.required_concession: This is a proposed formal analogy, not a proven mathematical identity.

claims.claim_text: The quaternion EM/Trinity isomorphism is Lean 4 verified with 478 theorems and zero sorry.
claims.support: Quaternion EM / Trinity isomorphism: Lean 4 verified, 478 theorems, zero sorry.
risks: Formal proof exists but may not be independently reviewed.
claims.required_concession: The formal proof is internal to the project; external verification is pending.

claims.support: Time is something the Trinity does, not a medium they inhabit.
claims.required_concession: This is a theological assertion, not a physical theory.

claims.claim_text: The nine fruits of the Spirit are the character of God Himself, existing eternally in the Trinity.
claims.support: The fruits are not a to-do list... They are the character of God Himself.
claims.required_concession: This is a theological claim based on scripture.

claims.claim_text: The four debts are the price of admission to thinking at all.
claims.support: The price of admission to thinking at all.
risks: Rhetorical flourish; not a formal claim.
claims.required_concession: This is a rhetorical statement, not a logical necessity.

claims.claim_text: The denial of orientation is an act of orientation.
claims.support: Anyone who calls any claim false has already assumed the gradient.
risks: Self-referential argument; may be seen as a performative contradiction.
claims.required_concession: This is a self-referential argument; its force depends on the assumption that truth is better than falsehood.

claims.claim_text: The Trinity mapping A1=Father, A2=Son, A3=Spirit, A4=Truth is locked.
claims.support: Trinity mapping: A1=Father (Existence), A2=Son (Distinction), A3=Spirit (Relation), A4=Truth (Orientation).
risks: Mapping is theological; not formally proven.
claims.required_concession: This mapping is a theological interpretation, not a formal derivation.

claims.claim_text: The derivative terms T.1–T.7 are newly derived and have NOT been through adversarial testing.
claims.support: The derivative terms T.1–T.7 are newly derived (July 2026) and have NOT been through adversarial testing at the term level.
risks: None; this is an honest admission.

claims.claim_text: T.4 (Omniscience) requires a formal bridge from coupling invariant to Shannon mutual information.
claims.support: T.4 (Omniscience): Formal bridge from coupling invariant → Shannon mutual information needed.
claims.required_concession: This is an open problem, not a proven claim.

claims.claim_text: T.7 (Love as Ground State) is a structural analogy, not necessarily the same force.
claims.support: Same form, but is it the SAME force or structural analogy?
claims.required_concession: This is an open question; the analogy is not yet established as identity.

claims.claim_text: The n ≥ 4 bound in Watcher is parsimony, not proof.
claims.support: n ≥ 4 bound in Watcher is parsimony, not proof.
risks: None; this is an honest admission.

fixes.problem: The truth operator is presented as a formal product but lacks mathematical definition.
fixes.repair: Either define the operator rigorously or explicitly label it as a theological analogy.

fixes.problem: The mapping of the four debts to the Trinity is theological and not formally derived.
fixes.repair: Add a concession that this is a theological interpretation, not a formal derivation.

fixes.problem: The claim 'time is authored' is ambiguous and could be misinterpreted as a physical theory.
fixes.repair: Clarify that this is a theological statement about God's relation to time, not a physical model.

log_notes: The work contains a mix of theological axioms, philosophical arguments, and formal claims. The formal claims (Lean verification) are strong but need external review.
The physics bridges (T.4, T.7) are explicitly open and should not be presented as proven.
The truth operator is a proposed formalism and should be treated as a hypothesis, not a theorem.
The document includes a clear boundary section listing what is locked and what is open, which is helpful for meta-analysis.
